# TestPion

> TestPion is a local-first desktop app and CLI for testing REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, MCP and AI/LLM systems, similar to Postman: collections, environments, Postman-compatible scripts (`tp.*`, with `pm.*` also running), a Collection Runner, mock servers, a cookie jar and Markdown docs, plus evaluations for LLM, RAG and agent tests. Everything runs on the user's machine; secrets are stored in the OS credential store and redacted from logs, traces, reports and exports. The `testpion` CLI runs collections like Newman (`testpion run-collection`) and serves a workspace to AI agents over MCP (`testpion mcp-server`).

Key facts for agents:

- Workspaces are folders of JSON/YAML files (`workspace.json`, `collections/*.json`, `environments/*.json`, `tests/**/*.yaml`) that can be committed to git. Secret values are never in these files.
- CLI JSON envelope (since 0.46): every `--json` output is `{ schema_version, command, status, data, errors, warnings, metrics }`; read `.data` (`testpion collections --json | jq '.data'`). `status` follows the exit code (`ok` 0, `failed` 1, `error` 2/3); `errors: [{ code, message, hint, retryable }]`. With `--json` stdout holds only JSON. `--jsonl` streams one line per event (`{ schema_version, command, type, data }`), the envelope last; `--dry-run` on a writing command lists `dry_run: { applied: false, changes: [{ path, change, bytes }] }`; `--non-interactive` (the default with `CI` or `TESTPION_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`) never waits for input.
- Production guard: an environment with `"isProduction": true` refuses data-changing requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, GraphQL mutations, non-read gRPC, realtime messages, MCP tool calls, `tp.sendRequest`) unless consented: CLI `--allow-production` on `test`, `run`, `run-collection`, `send`, `load`, `eval run`, `serve flows`, `ai attempt-fix` and `monitor add|run|start` (without it those steps fail with "needs confirmation"; reads still run); the MCP server needs `--allow-production` AND `allowProduction: true` on each sending call. `testpion ci` has no flag: add `--allow-production` to the generated run line (MCP `ci_config` takes `allowProduction`). Docs: /api-testing/environments#production
- MCP tool contract: tools that delete or overwrite need `confirm: true` (else they answer what they would do); lists page with `limit` (default 100, max 500) / `cursor` → `nextCursor`; big results are concise unless `response_format: "detailed"`; ids are snake_case (`run_id`); run/send/check tools declare `outputSchema`.
- Item refs: results that name an item carry `ref: { kind, …ids }`. `testpion search <words> [-n 20] --json` / MCP `search_workspace` find items; MCP `resolve_ref` checks a ref (a `testpion://open?…` link, `next` when gone) and `item_info` gives an item's file, variable names and latest runs; `testpion open <ref|kind:id|testpion://…> [--json|--print|--no-check]` opens it in the app (exit 2 when gone). `testpion problems [--json|--markdown]` (alias `attention`) or MCP `what_needs_attention` lists unreadable files, failing monitors, the latest failed run, failing requests, expiring certificates and flaky tests (exit 1 on a high-severity item).
- Item kinds: `testpion kinds [kind] [--all] [--json]` (MCP `list_kinds`) lists every kind of item a workspace holds (collection, request, test, flow, spec, dataset, mcp-server, monitor, run, history …) and what each offers: each capability is `true`, `{ na: why }` or `{ planned: release }` (do not rely on a planned one); `nodes` gives the app's row menus (groups in the order create, open, tree, run, share, tools, git, edit, danger). In the app every tree/list row has that one menu (right-click, ⋯, Shift+F10); F2 renames, Delete deletes with Undo. Docs: /getting-started/finding-your-way#menus
- Test types: http, graphql, grpc, websocket (or socketio / mqtt: connect, `send` messages / `{event,args,ack}` / `{topic,payload,qos,retain}` after `subscribe: [filters]`, assert on `$.received[n]`), mcp, llm, rag, agent, delay (`type: delay, ms: 2000`: a pause in a flow, 0–600000 ms, honours dependsOn, cancellable), condition (`type: condition, if: "status == 200"`; branches depend on it with `when: true|false`, the other is skipped), script (`type: script, script: "tp.variables.set('x', 1)"`), flow (`type: flow, file: other.yaml, inputs: {…}`: a sub-flow; its `output:` comes back), log (`type: log, message: "{{x}}"`), set (`type: set, set: { name: "{{template}}" }, scope: run|environment|collection|global`: scoped values kept like `tp.environment.set`), assert (`type: assert, assertions: [...], subject: response|variables`: checks only), wait (a request with `until:`). Any step: `if: <expression>`, `repeat: N`, `forEach: [rows] | { dataset: path }` ({{$index}}, {{$item}}, row fields), `finally: true` (clean-up after every other step, whatever happened), `parallel: <group>` (steps of a group may run together; unordered steps already run concurrently up to --concurrency). Any request: `until: { if: "$.status == 'done'", every: 2s, timeout: 60s, backoff: 1.5 }` (polls; fails "condition not met within …"). File top: `output: { name: "{{template}}" }`.
- Debug a flow: `testpion flow runs <file> [--run <runId>] --json` or MCP `flow_runs` (history; one run's steps with the variables after each, values cut at 4 KB, secrets redacted); re-run part of it with `testpion test <file> --from <step> [--seed-run <runId>]` / `--to <step>`, or MCP `run_tests` with `paths: [file]`, `from`, `seedRunId` (alone: replay from the first failing step). Breakpoints and pinned responses are the app designer's (`.local/flows/`), never used by the CLI, CI or MCP.
- Flows and auth: an HTTP step without `auth:` runs with the file's `defaults: auth:` (also a step written with a nested `request:`); `auth: { type: none }` sends one step without it. `testpion flow <file> [-e env] [--json|--dot]` and MCP `flow_graph` show the graph and its checks (unset variables, steps that never run, cycles) and `inheritedAuth: { <stepId>: { auth, from: "defaults", overridden? } }` (typed-in credentials as `***`).
- Edit a flow from the CLI / MCP: `testpion flow edit <file> --op '<json or list>' [--dry-run] --json` (ops addStep, updateStep, removeStep, renameStep, connect/disconnect with `when`, setOutput, setWebhook, setInputs, duplicateStep, group, addFromCollection, notes and frames …); shorthands `--connect a --to b [--when true|false]`, `--remove`, `--output`, `--parallel g --steps a,b`, `--finally`, `--webhook [path] --webhook-secret '{{S}}'`, `--no-webhook`. MCP `flow_add_step`, `flow_connect`, `flow_disconnect`, `flow_update_step`, `flow_remove_step` (confirm), `flow_set_output`, `flow_annotate`.
- Record a flow: `testpion flow from-har <file.har> [-o tests/x.yaml] [-e env] [--dry-run] --json` or MCP `flow_from_exchanges` (captured `ids` / `since`, or `har`): ids and tokens become extracts + dependsOn, noise is dropped, secrets become variables. Captured traffic as saved requests: `testpion debug --save-collection [name]` or MCP `debugger_save_to_collection`.
- Deploy a flow: `webhook: { path: /hooks/x, secret: "{{S}}" }` + `testpion serve flows -w <ws> [-e env] [--port 4020] [--host] [--jsonl]` (POST JSON body = inputs, answer `{ ok, output, steps, runId }`, 422 failed step, 401 secret; MCP `flow_webhook_set`); monitors run test files (`monitor add --test-file`); MCP `flow_deploy_status` says where a flow runs (monitor, webhook, MCP tool via `expose:`, CI).
- Flows at scale: `testpion test <flow> --data <csv|json|jsonl|sqlite|postgres://…|mysql://…> [--data-query sql] [--data-concurrency n] [--bail] --json` (rows in `.data.rows`; `{{$row.col}}`, `{{$index}}`), `testpion test <flow> --env-matrix dev,staging`, `testpion load --test-file <flow>` (MCP `load_test` `test_file`), `testpion flow report <file> [--run id] [--html out.html] --json` (timeline, critical path). MCP `flow_data_run`, `flow_env_matrix`, `flow_scale_result`, `flow_timeline`.
- Arazzo 1.0: `testpion import x.arazzo.yaml -w <ws> [--fetch-sources]` (one flow per workflow under tests/arazzo/), `testpion flow export <file> --arazzo [--spec specs/x.yaml] [-o out]`; MCP `import_arazzo` / `export_arazzo`.
- An integration flow from a collection or folder: `testpion flow generate --collection <name|id> [--folder <name|path|id>] [--hint "…"] [--privacy metadata] [--dry-run] [--apply] [--no-ai] --json`, MCP `flow_generate` (then `ai_apply_proposal`). Steps use the saved requests by id (invented ones are dropped with a note): create, read, update, delete, values extracted and passed on, status and key-field checks, error cases. Without a model it returns the deterministic draft; `--apply` writes only when verification did not fail.
- Same request, two environments: `testpion env diff <a> <b> --request <name> --json` or MCP `compare_request_across_environments` (response diff).
- Environment drift: `testpion env diff <a> <b> --json` (exit 1 when they differ) or MCP `compare_environments` (statuses only, no values).
- Proxy: the CLI honours HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY (TESTPION_NO_PROXY=1 disables); the app has Settings ▸ Proxy (env, custom URL + bypass list, or off).
- Private / corporate CAs: app Settings ▸ Certificates (OS store, extra PEM); CLI TESTPION_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1, TESTPION_CA_FILE=path or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.
- Deleting a collection, environment, dataset or MCP server moves it to the workspace trash for 30 days, and so does an API definition replaced by an import (`--replace-spec`): `testpion trash list|restore <id>|empty --yes -w <ws> [--json]`. Any such item by its ref: `testpion item delete <ref> -w <ws> [--json]` (`collection:<id>`, `environment:<id>`, `dataset:<name>`, `spec:specs/<path>`, `mcp-server:<id>`; prints the trash id) and `testpion item restore <trashId>` (a taken name gets "(restored)"); MCP `delete_item` (`ref`, `confirm: true`) / `restore_item` (`trash_id`); a request of a collection: `delete_request`. A kind that cannot be trashed is refused with the reason.
- AI: the user's own Anthropic key (app Settings ▸ AI assistant, kept in the OS secret store; CLI/CI: TESTPION_SECRET_APP_ANTHROPIC_APIKEY) adds the provider `claude-app` (Claude Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 4.5) to every workspace.
- TestPion's own AI tasks (explain, suggest checks, write tp tests, write a flow, triage, analyze flaky …) run through one engine with the model the user configured (their Claude key, a workspace provider, or a local Ollama / LM Studio). CLI: `testpion ai tasks --json`, `testpion ai run <task> --item <ref> [-q …] [--privacy full|metadata|names] [--dry-run] [--json]` (refs: `request:<collectionId>:<requestId>`, `run:<id>:<resultId>`, `history:<id>`, `test:<path>`, `flow:<path>`, `spec:<path>`, `collection:<id>`, `folder:<c>:<f>`); MCP `ai_list_tasks`, `ai_run_task` (`dryRun: true` returns what would be sent and the estimate, sends nothing). Suggested checks: `ai run suggest-assertions` (alias of `generate-assertions`); a check that pins a changing value is flagged with safer forms.
- Generating AI tasks never write: they return a proposal (`ai-…` id, kept a day in `.local/ai/proposals/`) whose items were verified (checks run against the stored response, tp tests in the sandbox, test files linted, flows run on a mock of the collection). Apply after the user agrees: `testpion ai apply <id> [--items i1,i3]` or MCP `ai_apply_proposal` (needs `confirm: true`; `dryRun: true` lists what it would write); undo with `testpion ai undo <id>` / `ai_undo_proposal`; list with `testpion ai proposals --json` / `ai_proposals`.
- AI model for the CLI/CI: `--provider/--model`, else `TESTPION_AI_PROVIDER` (a workspace provider id or name, `ollama`, `mock`, `anthropic` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `openai-compatible` + `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `claude-app` + `TESTPION_SECRET_APP_ANTHROPIC_APIKEY`), `TESTPION_AI_MODEL`, `TESTPION_AI_MODEL_SMALL` / `_LARGE`, else the app's Settings ▸ AI assistant (the MCP server uses those). `TESTPION_AI_LOCAL_ONLY=1` refuses any model that is not on this computer before anything is sent. What is sent is always redacted (secret values, sensitive field names, credentials found by shape, personal data); privacy level `metadata` sends no body values, `names` less; variable names may be sent, values never.
- AI usage and caps: every AI call (app, CLI, MCP, CI) is recorded: `testpion ai usage [--days N] --json`, MCP `ai_usage`. Caps (tokens per call, tokens and cost per day) are in Settings ▸ AI assistant ▸ Limits; a call over a cap, with the assistant off, or with Local only on fails with nothing sent (exit 2).
- Failed run to causes and fixes: `testpion ai triage --run <id|last> --json` (MCP `ai_triage_run`) groups failures without AI (same check, status, endpoint), then the model explains each cause with evidence and a fix verified against the failing and the last passing response; it returns a proposal, nothing is written until `ai apply`. `--no-ai` or no model: the grouping with likely causes only. CI: `testpion test|run|run-collection … --triage` writes triage.md / triage.json next to the results and never changes the exit code.
- Flaky test: `testpion ai run analyze-flaky --item test:<path>[:<step>]` (or `test-case:<testId>` from `testpion history flaky --json` / MCP `flaky_tests`), MCP `ai_analyze_flaky`; the fix never hides a failure (an `until:` wait, a stable check, isolated data). `testpion ai attempt-fix <id> [--times 5] --json` / MCP `ai_attempt_fix` (asks the user) applies it and runs the test N times: `attempt.verdict` = stable | flaky | failing.
- `testpion run-collection <collection of the workspace>` records what it ran, so `ci --run last`, `--rerun-failed` and `ai triage --run last` work on it (`--rerun-failed` sends only the failed requests; a token set by an earlier request is not there, so add it with `--folder` or `--env-var`).
- `testpion load --collection <name> -w <ws> [--folder <f>] [--warm-up]` load-tests a collection (each virtual user runs its requests in order; per-request latency in the results). gRPC: `testpion load host:port --grpc pkg.Service/Method -d '{json}'` (reflection or --proto). MCP `load_test` does the same for local hosts (≤ 50 users, ≤ 60 s). Thresholds: `--threshold "p95<500" "errors<1%" "rps>=50" "p99[Request]<800"` (exit 1 when one fails; MCP `thresholds`).
- `testpion vars usages <name> -w <ws> --json` and `testpion vars rename <from> <to> -w <ws>` find and rename a variable everywhere (MCP `variable_usages`, `rename_variable`).
- `testpion export <collection> --format openapi [--json]` writes an OpenAPI 3.1 document for a collection (MCP `collection_openapi`).
- `testpion record <target> [--port] [-w <ws> --collection <name>]` records traffic through a localhost reverse proxy and saves it as a collection (responses as examples, secrets as {{variables}}). In the app the same reverse proxy is a capture mode of the HTTP Debugger (rows with `source: "reverse"`), so Create flow, Save to collection and HAR export work on them.
- `testpion lint <collection> -w <ws> [--fail-on high] [--json]` is a security review of a collection's requests (MCP `security_review`); the `security-headers` check tests responses.
- GraphQL subscriptions: `testpion graphql-subscribe <endpoint> -q <doc> [--max n] [--json]` (MCP `graphql_subscribe`), graphql-transport-ws and graphql-ws.
- GraphQL operation builder: `testpion graphql-op Query.field --endpoint <url> | --schema <file> [--depth n] [--json]` (MCP `graphql_operation`) returns a valid query with typed variables and placeholder values; in the app, **Build** on a root field of the schema explorer.
- `testpion send "<Collection/Request>"|<url> -w <ws> -e <env> [--json] [--fail]` sends one request (saved requests run their scripts and checks; a URL target resolves `{{variables}}` only with `-w <ws>`).
- `testpion env set <env> key=value … -w <ws> [--create]` / `env unset` / `env get` edit plain environment variables (MCP `set_environment_variable`); secrets are only set in the app. `--also-in Staging,Production [--copy]` sets it in other environments too (MCP `alsoIn`, `copyValues`).
- Newman command lines work with `newman run` replaced by `testpion run-collection` (same -e, -g, -d, -n, --folder, --env-var, --global-var, --export-environment, --export-globals, -k, --suppress-exit-code, --reporters, --reporter-junit-export). Scripts have lodash (`_`), `moment`, `tv4` and real `jsonSchema` checks, as in Postman.
- Dynamic variables use Postman's names: `{{$guid}}`, `{{$timestamp}}`, `{{$isoTimestamp}}`, `{{$randomInt(1,10)}}`, `{{$randomFirstName}}`, `{{$randomEmail}}` (example.test) and ~70 more `{{$random…}}` values; each use gives a new value.
- `testpion openapi-diff <old> <new> [--json] [--fail-on-breaking]` lists breaking changes between two OpenAPI versions (files or links); MCP `openapi_diff` does the same.
- `testpion load --saved <name> [-e env] [--threshold rule...]` runs a load test saved in the app (target, users, duration, rules); `{{variables}}` in any load URL resolve from `-e`.
- `testpion eval list [--json]` and `testpion eval run <name> [-e env] [--limit n]` list and run evaluations saved in the app (dataset × prompt × model × evaluators); MCP `list_evaluations` / `run_evaluation` do the same. Compare runs: `testpion eval compare <run|last|name> --baseline <run> [--threshold 0.05] [--max-regressions 0] [--fail-on-missing] --json` (exit 1 on regressions; for CI) and `testpion eval matrix <runs...> [--baseline r] [--filter failed|regressed|improved|changed|missing] [--tag t] [--sort score|delta|failures] [--offset n --limit n] --json` (MCP `eval_compare`, `eval_matrix`).
- `testpion coverage <spec> [--run <id...>] [--history [n]] [--min <pct>] [--json]` reports which OpenAPI operations and documented response codes the latest run (or given runs / request history) exercised, never-called operations and undocumented codes; MCP `api_coverage` returns the same JSON. Use it to find untested endpoints and error cases, then write tests for them.
- `testpion import <file|url|-> -w <ws> --json` imports from a file, stdin, or an http(s) link (OpenAPI URL, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket file page, Postman API link).
- .env files import as environments (secret-looking keys become secret variables) and environments export as .env.
- CI: `testpion ci <github|gitlab|azure|jenkins> -w <ws> [--suite s | --collection c [--folder f]] [-e env] --json` (or MCP `ci_config`) returns { path, content, secrets, command } in the envelope's `data`; `--run <runId|last>` builds it from a run, and for one flow `--tests <file> [--data [file] | --env-matrix a b] [--timeline-html]` keeps `test-results/data-run.json` / `env-matrix.json` and `timeline.html`. The pipeline installs the CLI from github.com/nasimuddin-dev/testpion at the version's tag (the CLI is not on npm).
- A complete example workspace against free public APIs is at `examples/public-workspace` (REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, SSE, MCP, AI; suites `all` and `offline`); the desktop app opens it on first launch. Docs: /getting-started/examples
- OpenTelemetry: `testpion test|run-collection --trace all --otlp http://collector:4318` (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT/HEADERS) sends traces as OTLP/HTTP JSON; MCP `export_traces`; Traces view ▸ Send to OpenTelemetry.
- Scripts may use top-level `await`: `const res = await tp.sendRequest(url)`; `await tp.vault.get('key')` and `{{vault:key}}` read (secret) variables.
- MCP client features: `type: mcp` tests answer server requests with `elicitation: { action, content }`, `sampling: "reply"`, `roots: [paths]`; the inspector shows elicitation forms and sampling review dialogs.
- Scripts have cheerio (`const $ = cheerio.load(tp.response.text()); $('title').text()`), lodash, moment, tv4, crypto-js, xml2Json.
- Script packages: `tp.require('@team/utils')` loads workspace file packages/@team/utils.js (CommonJS, module.exports), like Postman's package library.
- Save as test: **Save as test…** in a request's ⋯, the Collections menu (a folder or collection becomes one file), History, Debugger rows and the MCP view writes tests/<kind>/<name>.yaml; CLI `testpion test from-request "Collection/Folder/Request" | <ref> [-n name] --json`; MCP `save_test` (`ref`, or collection + request).
- MCP `list_tests` / `run_tests` (paths, grep, tags, rerunFailed) run the YAML tests under tests/.
- Re-run only failures: `testpion test --rerun-failed [runId]` (default last run).
- Saving outputs (app): every response and result has one down arrow at the right end of its bar (Copy · Download · ▾ formats; Ctrl+Shift+S, or File ▸ Download Output…): JSON, JSON Lines, raw bytes, text, CSV, TSV, HTML, Markdown, XML, HAR, cURL (.sh), JUnit XML, cookies.txt, ZIP, with safe file names. Logs, run results and reports, traces, timelines, the HAR and the cURL command are masked of secrets when recorded; "Include secrets…" (after a confirmation) is only for outputs that hold them (decoded JWTs, the terminal transcript). Big outputs stream from disk; CSV cells starting with = + - @ get a leading `'`. From the CLI: `-o <dir> -r junit json html markdown` on `test` / `run-collection` / `eval run`, `report`, `load --json <file>`, `history export-har -o`, `debug -o <file.har>`, `flow report --html`; anything else prints to stdout. Docs: /getting-started/save-and-export-results
- Watch mode for local development: `testpion test --watch`, `testpion run-collection <c> --watch` re-run on file changes.
- Imports (app, `testpion import <file> -w <ws> --json`): OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2, Postman v2.1, Insomnia v4/v5 (request and folder scripts; template tags `{% uuid/now/timestamp/faker %}` become dynamic variables, `{% base64/hash %}` a pre-request line, `{% response %}` a chained variable), Bruno (collection folder of .bru files, a .bru file, or JSON export; `bru.*` scripts rewritten to `tp.*`, assertions become tests, the collection's `.env` becomes secret variables of a "Bruno .env" environment), Hoppscotch, GraphQL SDL (`.graphql`: a request for `{{graphqlUrl}}`, schema kept in specs/graphql/), WSDL 1.1 (SOAP 1.1/1.2 requests with SOAPAction and sample envelopes from the XSD; file or ?wsdl link), HAR, cURL/fetch/PowerShell snippets. Export back: `testpion export <c> --format bruno --out <dir>` writes a Bruno folder (scripts written with `bru.*`).
- Import notes: every import returns `notes` (what did not map one to one, naming the request): unsupported auth (Hawk, NTLM, EdgeGrid, ASAP, WSSE, netrc, JWT RS256 …) becomes auth `none` plus a disabled `X-Imported-Auth-<Scheme>: needs manual setup` header, never inherit; `bru.*` calls without an equivalent are marked `// TODO(import)`. The CLI prints the first 20 under "Check after import"; `--json` and MCP `import_definition` return all.
- Spec imports never overwrite: an OpenAPI / AsyncAPI / GraphQL document whose `specs/` path holds a different document is saved as `name-2`; `testpion import <file> --replace-spec` replaces it (the old one goes to the trash). The same document imported again is not copied.
- Workspace export: `testpion workspace export <name|path> [-o file] [--json]` writes `<name>.testpion.json` (collections, environments, tests, saved items, MCP servers, providers and the files of specs/, datasets/, mocks/, protos/; files over 10 MB or past 50 MB in all are left out and listed in `notes`). It never contains a secret: typed-in tokens, secret headers, MCP server headers and env values, connection-string passwords and provider keys become `{{variables}}`, listed in `replaced`. Importing it lists `valuesNeeded`.
- Postman v2.1 collections and environments import and export losslessly where the formats overlap.
- `testpion collections --json` lists a workspace's collections (requests, gRPC calls, connections); `testpion requests <collection> --json` lists what one holds.
- Git: `testpion git sync` / MCP `git_sync` (confirm) pulls (collections merged request by request) and pushes in one step; exit 1 lists conflicts. `testpion diff <from> [to] --markdown` reads flows step by step.
- AGENTS.md: `testpion agents init [--targets agents,claude,cursor] [--dry-run] [--force] --json` (MCP `agents_init`) writes the workspace's AGENTS.md section between `<!-- testpion:begin -->` and `<!-- testpion:end -->` (plus a CLAUDE.md pointer and `.cursor/rules/testpion.mdc`).
- The app has a Terminal tab (Ctrl+`) in the workspace folder with `testpion` on the PATH; the MCP server over stdio is started as `TestPion --mcp-server` (Settings ▸ AI agents shows the command).
- To let an agent use a workspace, register the MCP server: `testpion mcp-server -w <workspace>` (stdio). Tools: `list_collections`, `list_requests`, `get_request`, `list_environments`, `collection_docs`, `send_request`, `run_collection`, `parse_request_snippet`, `save_request`, `import_definition` (from a url or text), `import_arazzo` / `export_arazzo` (Arazzo 1.0 workflows ↔ flow files; also `testpion import x.arazzo.yaml` and `testpion flow export <file> --arazzo`), `reorder_environments`, `list_flows` (flows with `expose:`), `mock_tools`, `list_datasets` / `read_dataset` / `add_dataset_row`, `run_reviews` / `review_result`, `generate_flows`. More than 120 tools in all (/ai-testing/mcp-server); `search_tools` finds the right one. Add `--read-only` to disable sending and saving, `--profile minimal` to list only the common tools (about 25).
- A request copied as cURL (bash or cmd), fetch or PowerShell can be parsed (`parse_request_snippet`), sent (`send_request` with `snippet`) or saved (`save_request`, or CLI `testpion import <file|-> -w <ws> --json`). Secrets in it are replaced by `{{variables}}` listed in `placeholders`; they are never written to workspace files.
- Scripts use the Postman API as `tp.*` (TestPion's name) or `pm.*` (Postman's): the same object, both always work. Exports to Postman convert `tp.*` to `pm.*`; `testpion scripts convert --to tp|pm --json` rewrites a workspace's scripts.
- Test scripts can call `tp.visualizer.set(template, data)` (Handlebars); run results include the rendered `visualization.html` and `scriptLogs`.
- Monitors (collections or test files / flows on a schedule): `testpion monitor add <name> --collection <c> | --test-file <path> --every 15m [--allow-production]`, `monitor list|results --json`, `monitor run --due` (cron) or `monitor start` (long-running); MCP `list_monitors` / `save_monitor` / `monitor_results` / `run_monitor`. Docs: /test-runner/monitors
- Response history: `testpion history list --request <name> --json` / `testpion history diff <before> <after> --json`, or MCP `request_history` / `compare_responses`, show what changed between two runs of a request (field-by-field JSON diff; secrets masked). `testpion history stats --request <name> --json` or MCP `response_time_stats` give its median / p95 / slowest response time and failure count. `testpion history list --kind capture [-q <text>] --json` (MCP `history_list` with `kind: "capture"`) lists the HTTP Debugger's capture sessions, each with `capture.ref` (a collection, a flow, or a saved `debugger/<name>.har`), its exchange count, `sources` (proxy / reverse) and hosts.
- `testpion env list --json` and `testpion env order <names...>` read and set the environment order.
- CLI exit codes: 0 success, 1 test failure, 2 configuration error (also a wrong argument), 3 execution error; the `--json` `status` mirrors it.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/installation): install the desktop app or the CLI
- [Your first request](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/first-request): send a request, add assertions, save it to a collection
- [Workspaces](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/workspaces): switch, rename, duplicate, export and delete workspaces; `testpion workspace list|rename|delete --json`, `testpion workspace export <name> --json` (secrets replaced by {{variables}})
- [What's new](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/whats-new): each release step by step, with the behaviour changes to read before upgrading
- [Import fidelity](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/import-fidelity): what each importer maps, the notes after an import, Insomnia template tags, Bruno scripts and .env
- [Finding your way around](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/finding-your-way): Quick Open, Problems, item refs and `testpion://open` links, menus, Delete with Undo; `testpion search` / `open` / `problems` / `kinds`
- [Save and export results](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/save-and-export-results): the down arrow, formats, secret masking, what the CLI writes
- [Keep your workspace in git](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/git): Pull & push, flows diffed step by step, `testpion git sync`
- [Terminal](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/terminal): the app's terminal tab with `testpion` on the PATH
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/keyboard-shortcuts): every shortcut on one page
- [Your first AI test](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/getting-started/first-ai-test): test an LLM prompt with evaluators

## API testing

- [REST and HTTP](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/rest): requests, responses, `tp.*` scripts, console, tabs, history, JSONPath filter suggestions and Diff vs previous
- [WebSocket, Socket.IO and MQTT](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/websocket): connect, send messages, emit Socket.IO events (with acknowledgements), subscribe and publish on MQTT brokers (3.1.1 and 5, QoS, retained); `testpion ws`, `testpion mqtt`; MCP tool `realtime_exchange` (`mode: mqtt`, `subscribe`); saved connections in folders; clear connection errors
- [Server-Sent Events](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/rest#server-sent-events): text/event-stream responses parsed event by event (live, Stop keeps events); MCP send_request returns them
- [OpenAPI contract testing](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/test-runner/assertions#openapi-contract-testing): the `openapi` check validates status, content type and body schema against an OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 document (`spec: openapi.yaml`)
- [Authentication](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/authentication): API key, Basic, Bearer, JWT, OAuth 1.0, OAuth 2.0, AWS Signature v4, Digest, mTLS
- [Environments and variables](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/environments): scopes and precedence, secrets, quick look, export
- [Cookies](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/cookies): the workspace cookie jar, `tp.cookies.jar()`, CLI cookie jar files
- [Mock servers](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/mock-servers): serve saved examples on localhost
- [HTTP Debugger](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/http-debugger): capture other programs' traffic, rules, HTTPS decryption, Save to collection, Record a flow; `testpion debug`
- [Environments: production](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/environments#production): the production guard, `--allow-production`, `allowProduction`
- [Collections](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/collections): import, export to Postman, examples, documentation, Collection Runner

## GraphQL and MCP

- [GraphQL overview](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/graphql/overview)
- [GraphQL mock server](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/graphql/mocking): `testpion mock-graphql --schema schema.graphql` serves fake, typed, deterministic data for any valid query
- [GraphQL testing](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/graphql/testing)
- [gRPC](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/api-testing/grpc): call gRPC services from .proto files or server reflection (unary and streaming), metadata, TLS, deadlines; `type: grpc` tests with `grpc-status`; `testpion grpc`; MCP tool `grpc_call`
- [MCP overview](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/mcp/overview): test MCP servers (stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE)
- [MCP tools](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/mcp/tools)
- [MCP mock server](https://nasimuddin-dev.github.io/testpion/mcp/mocking): fake MCP servers from `*.mcp-mock.yaml` (or recorded from a real server with Save as mock); `testpion mock-mcp <file>` serves one over stdio or `--http` for agents
